name: hlc-send-receive
description: The send and receive rules of §4.1, plus drift rejection (§4.5). Timestamps are given as (millis, counter) rather than encoded strings so the arithmetic is readable; encoding is covered by 01-encoding.json. `pt` is the physical wall clock the implementation must be driven with, which is why these vectors carry an explicit clock rather than reading the host's.

send.description: physical clock has advanced past the logical clock: adopt it and reset the counter
physical clock is behind (clock skew or two ops in one millisecond): keep millis, bump the counter
physical clock exactly equals millis: still a counter bump, because the rule is strictly greater
counter overflow rolls into the next millisecond rather than wrapping to a duplicate

receive.description: remote is ahead: adopt remote millis, counter is remote counter + 1
local is ahead: keep local millis, bump local counter
local and remote share the same millisecond: counter is max of both, plus one
physical clock is ahead of both: adopt it and reset the counter to zero
counter overflow on receive rolls into the next millisecond
remote exactly at the drift limit is accepted; the rule is strictly greater than pt + MAX_DRIFT
one millisecond beyond the drift limit is rejected, and the whole batch fails
a wildly future timestamp is rejected rather than poisoning LWW forever
